docs.x: Puerto Rico land mine. Court of Appeals: the fee payment date is the filing date: Uploading the appeal to SUMAC is not filing. The filing receipt warns that the document is not officially filed until the filing fees are paid, and the filing date is the fee payment date. It does not relate back to the upload. The 11:59 p.m. e-filing rule also does not apply to filings that require a fee. Pay on the platform the same day. If the trial case has no electronic record, also send the trial court clerk a stamped cover page within 72 hours (strict compliance). (Reglamento TA R. 14(A); Directrices SUMAC §§ VII, XVI(1))

docs.t: Puerto Rico — Serve the appellate brief on the other side within the filing period
docs.x: Puerto Rico land mine. Serve the appellate brief on the other side within the filing period: The appellant must serve the appeal and appendices on the other parties within the time to file the appeal (strict compliance) and certify the date of service. E-filing serves lawyers, but pro se parties and others the law requires must be served separately. (Reglamento TA R. 13(B))

docs.t: Puerto Rico — Summons must be served within 120 days, or the case is dismissed
docs.x: Puerto Rico land mine. Summons must be served within 120 days, or the case is dismissed: Serve the summons within 120 days of filing the complaint (or of issuance of a summons by publication). If service is not completed in time, the court must dismiss without prejudice. A second dismissal for the same failure operates as an adjudication on the merits. Service cannot be done through SUMAC. Out-of-island defendants may be served personally, under the law of the place of service, by letters rogatory, by publication, or as the court orders. (R. Proc. Civ. 4.3(b)-(c), 67.6)

docs.t: Puerto Rico — Nonresident plaintiffs must post a cost bond
docs.x: Puerto Rico land mine. Nonresident plaintiffs must post a cost bond: When the claimant lives outside Puerto Rico or is a foreign corporation, the court must require a bond of at least $1,000 for costs, expenses, and attorney’s fees, and all proceedings are stayed until it is posted. If it is not posted within 60 days of the order, the court dismisses the case. Narrow exceptions apply: indigent litigants exempt from filing fees, co-owners suing over Puerto Rico property alongside a resident co-owner, and partition of property located in Puerto Rico. (R. Proc. Civ. 69.5)

docs.t: Puerto Rico — Court of Appeals reconsideration: 15 days, no extensions
docs.x: Puerto Rico land mine. Court of Appeals reconsideration: 15 days, no extensions: A motion to reconsider a Court of Appeals decision, civil or criminal, is due within 15 days of archivo en autos of the notice, and the term cannot be extended. A timely motion stops the clock to go to the Supreme Court, which restarts when notice of the ruling on the motion is filed. (Reglamento TA R. 84(A); R. Proc. Civ. 52.2(f))

docs.t: Puerto Rico — Criminal appeals run from the date of sentencing
docs.x: Puerto Rico land mine. Criminal appeals run from the date of sentencing: A criminal appeal is due within 30 days after the sentence is pronounced, not after notice. The term is jurisdictional. A timely new-trial or reconsideration motion restarts the 30 days from notice of the order resolving it. Certiorari from a conviction on a guilty plea is also 30 days from the sentence, jurisdictional. (Reglamento TA R. 23(A), 32(A))

docs.t: Puerto Rico — Agency review: 30 days to the Court of Appeals
docs.x: Puerto Rico land mine. Agency review: 30 days to the Court of Appeals: Judicial review of a final agency order or decision goes directly to the Court of Appeals within 30 days (jurisdictional) of archivo en autos of the notice, or of the restarted date after a timely agency reconsideration motion, unless a special law sets a different term. (Reglamento TA R. 57)

docs.t: Puerto Rico — Pro hac vice counsel cannot e-file and must bring local counsel everywhere
docs.x: Puerto Rico land mine. Pro hac vice counsel cannot e-file and must bring local counsel everywhere: A courtesy-admitted lawyer has no SUMAC filing access and must file on paper. The endorsing Puerto Rico lawyer must sign every filing and attend every hearing and deposition unless excused. Budget for full local-counsel participation, not a name on the signature block. (Reglamento TS R. 12(f)(2); Directrices SUMAC § V(3))

docs.t: Puerto Rico — Withdrawal needs leave of court
docs.x: Puerto Rico land mine. Withdrawal needs leave of court: Counsel who has appeared must move in writing to withdraw, give reasons, provide the client’s phone and mailing address, and certify the client was notified. The court may refuse in exceptional cases if a party’s rights would be seriously harmed or the case unduly delayed. (R. Proc. Civ. 9.2)

docs.t: Puerto Rico anti-SLAPP — Status not confirmed from the collected texts
docs.x: Puerto Rico anti-SLAPP. Status not confirmed from the collected texts: The collected Puerto Rico court texts (civil and criminal procedure, evidence, court rules, ethics rules, e-filing guidelines) contain no anti-SLAPP procedure: no special motion to dismiss, no discovery stay, and no fee-shifting rule tied to speech or petitioning. An anti-SLAPP law, if one exists, would be a statute outside these rules. Before telling a client anything, search the Leyes de Puerto Rico Anotadas (LPRA) and the Oficina de Gerencia y Presupuesto virtual library (bvirtualogp.pr.gov) for any enacted law on strategic lawsuits against public participation, and confirm its number, effective date, and procedure. No statute is named here because none could be verified. (None verified; check LPRA and enacted laws (Leyes) for any anti-SLAPP statute)

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Civil appeal (apelación) to the TA
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Civil appeal (apelación) to the TA: 30 days from Archivo en autos of the copy of the notice of judgment (SUMAC send date; mailing date if later) (Regla 13(A) Reglamento TA; Regla 52.2(a) R. Proc. Civ.). Jurisdictional. Restarts after a timely Rule 43.1, 47 or 48 motion is decided and notified.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Civil appeal to the TA when the government is a party
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Civil appeal to the TA when the government is a party: 60 days from Archivo en autos of the copy of the notice of judgment (Regla 13(A) Reglamento TA; Regla 52.2(c) R. Proc. Civ.). Jurisdictional. Applies to any aggrieved party when the ELA, its officials, a non-public-corporation instrumentality, or a municipality or its officials is a party.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Certiorari to the TA against interlocutory orders (civil or criminal), protection orders, and judgments on arb
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Certiorari to the TA against interlocutory orders (civil or criminal), protection orders, and judgments on arbitration-award review: 30 days from Archivo en autos of the copy of the notice of the order (Civ. Rule 52.2(b) says “fecha de notificación”) (Regla 32(C) Reglamento TA; Regla 52.2(b) R. Proc. Civ.). Strict compliance: excusable only for special circumstances explained in the petition. No 60-day government extension.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Certiorari to the TA against final resolutions in jurisdicción voluntaria
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Certiorari to the TA against final resolutions in jurisdicción voluntaria: 30 days from Archivo en autos of the copy of the notice of the resolution (Regla 32(B) Reglamento TA; Regla 52.2(b) R. Proc. Civ.). Jurisdictional, unless a special law sets another term.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Certiorari to the TA against a guilty-plea conviction
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Certiorari to the TA against a guilty-plea conviction: 30 days from Date the sentence was dictated (mailing date of notice if the defendant was not present) (Regla 32(A) Reglamento TA; Regla 193 R. Proc. Crim.). Jurisdictional. Criminal rules compilation current only to Feb. 2020.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Criminal appeal to the TA
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Criminal appeal to the TA: 30 days from Date the sentence was dictated; or notice of the order denying a timely new-trial motion (Rules 188(e), 192) or deciding a timely reconsideration (Regla 23(A) Reglamento TA; Regla 194 R. Proc. Crim.). Jurisdictional. Regla 23 counts from notice to the accused of the ruling; Rule 194 counts a reconsideration ruling from its archivo en autos. Criminal rules compilation current only to Feb. 2020.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Recurso de revisión (final agency decision) to the TA
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Recurso de revisión (final agency decision) to the TA: 30 days from Archivo en autos of the copy of the notice of the final order (mailing date if later), or the applicable date after a timely reconsideration (Regla 57 Reglamento TA). Jurisdictional unless a special law provides otherwise. Agency reconsideration terms are in the LPAU, not reviewed here.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Recurso de revisión especial (welfare benefits, pro se)
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Recurso de revisión especial (welfare benefits, pro se): 30 days from Receipt of the agency’s final order (Regla 67(C) Reglamento TA). Only for self-represented persons challenging welfare-benefit decisions.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Electoral certiorari to the TA (CEE cases)
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Electoral certiorari to the TA (CEE cases): 10 days from Archivo en autos of the copy of the notice of the TPI judgment (or of the ruling on reconsideration) (Regla 42 Reglamento TA). Jurisdictional. Within 30 days before an election: 48 hours. Within 5 days before: 24 hours, with same-day notice. No reconsideration in those windows.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Serve the recurso and appendix on the other parties (TA)
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Serve the recurso and appendix on the other parties (TA): Within the filing term days from Same trigger as the recurso (Reglas 13(B)(1), 23(B), 33(B) y 58(B)(1) Reglamento TA). Strict compliance. E-filing serves counsel; you must serve self-represented and other required parties.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Notify the TPI when its case has no electronic record
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Notify the TPI when its case has no electronic record: 72 hours (civil appeal); 48 hours (criminal appeal, certiorari) days from Filing of the recurso (Reglas 14(A), 24(A) y 33(A) Reglamento TA). Strict compliance. Not needed when SUMAC posts the entry automatically in an electronic TPI record.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Send the original to the TA after filing on paper at the TPI
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Send the original to the TA after filing on paper at the TPI: 48 hours days from Filing at the TPI Secretaría (Reglas 14(C), 24(B) y 33(A) Reglamento TA). Strict compliance. Only when paper filing is allowed under Regla 2.1.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Supplementary certification of service
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Supplementary certification of service: 48 hours (3 business days in revisión) days from Filing of the recurso (Reglas 15 y 58(B)(4) Reglamento TA). Strict compliance.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Late appendix documents, with leave
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Late appendix documents, with leave: 15 days from Notice of the TA resolution allowing late filing (Reglas 16(E)(2) y 34(E)(2) Reglamento TA). Failure to cure may lead to dismissal.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Notice of intent to reproduce oral evidence
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Notice of intent to reproduce oral evidence: 10 days from Filing of the recurso (Reglas 19(B), 29(B) y 76(A) Reglamento TA). Identify portions, dates and witnesses, and the method proposed.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Motion in the TPI or agency for the re-recording (regrabación)
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Motion in the TPI or agency for the re-recording (regrabación): 10 days from Notice of the TA order authorizing reproduction (Regla 76(B) Reglamento TA). Pay the fees with the motion.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Transcript of oral evidence
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Transcript of oral evidence: 30 days from Delivery of the re-recording (Regla 76(C) Reglamento TA). Or the term the TA orders; extendable only for good cause by a reasoned motion. Serve copies within the same term.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Stipulated narrative statement: draft, then negotiation
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Stipulated narrative statement: draft, then negotiation: 30, then 20 days from TA authorization; then service of the draft (Regla 76(D) Reglamento TA). If no agreement, the other side files specific objections.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Supplementary brief after transcript or narrative (civil appeal)
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Supplementary brief after transcript or narrative (civil appeal): 30 days from Filing of the transcript or narrative statement (Regla 21 Reglamento TA). Announce it when filing the transcript. The appellee may reply within 30 days.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Appellee’s brief, civil appeal (TA)
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Appellee’s brief, civil appeal (TA): 30 days from Filing of the escrito de apelación; or filing of the reproduced oral evidence if any is brought up (Regla 22 Reglamento TA). May include its own appendix.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Opposition to certiorari (TA)
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Opposition to certiorari (TA): 10 days from Notification of the petition (Regla 37(A) Reglamento TA). 25 pages paper / 35 electronic.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Respondent’s brief after the TA issues certiorari
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Respondent’s brief after the TA issues certiorari: 30 days from Notice of issuance of the writ (Regla 39(A) Reglamento TA). Extendable. The petition is the petitioner’s brief.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Opposition brief in administrative revisión
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Opposition brief in administrative revisión: 30 days from Notification of the recurso (Regla 63(A) Reglamento TA). Due from the agency, the official and other parties.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Criminal appellant’s brief; then El Pueblo’s brief
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Criminal appellant’s brief; then El Pueblo’s brief: 30, then 30 days from Elevation of the record; then filing of the appellant’s brief (Regla 28(A), (E) Reglamento TA). Unless the TA orders otherwise.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Response to a motion (TA)
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Response to a motion (TA): 10 days from Notification of the motion (Regla 68(B) Reglamento TA). The TA may rule sooner in extraordinary circumstances.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Request for an extension (TA or TS)
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Request for an extension (TA or TS): At least 3 business days before the term expires days from Expiration of the term (Regla 72(B) Reglamento TA; Regla 48(b) Reglamento TS). Never available for jurisdictional terms.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Panel review of a single judge’s habeas corpus or mandamus resolution
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Panel review of a single judge’s habeas corpus or mandamus resolution: 10 days from Archivo en autos of the notice of the resolution (Regla 55(H) Reglamento TA).

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Reconsideration of a TPI civil judgment
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Reconsideration of a TPI civil judgment: 15 days from Archivo en autos of the copy of the notice of judgment (Regla 47 R. Proc. Civ.). Jurisdictional. Serve the other parties within the same 15 days (strict compliance). Must be specific or it does not interrupt.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Reconsideration of a TPI interlocutory order
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Reconsideration of a TPI interlocutory order: 15 days from Notice of the order (Regla 47 R. Proc. Civ.). Strict compliance.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Reconsideration of a criminal sentence or conviction (TPI)
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Reconsideration of a criminal sentence or conviction (TPI): 15 days from Date the sentence was dictated (Regla 194 R. Proc. Crim.). Not extendable. Criminal rules compilation current only to Feb. 2020.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Reconsideration in the TA
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Reconsideration in the TA: 15 days from Archivo en autos of the copy of the notice of the TA decision (Regla 84(A) Reglamento TA; Regla 216 R. Proc. Crim.). Not extendable. Suspends the term to go to the TS. Opposition within 10 days. Electoral cases: 10 days under Regla 42.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Certiorari to the TS against a TA judgment in an appeal
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Certiorari to the TS against a TA judgment in an appeal: 30 days from Archivo en autos of the copy of the notice (or of the ruling on reconsideration; mailing date if later) (Regla 20(a)(1), (c) Reglamento TS; Regla 52.2(b) R. Proc. Civ.). Jurisdictional. 60 days in civil cases where the government is a party.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Certiorari to the TS against TA rulings on guilty-plea certiorari, jurisdicción voluntaria, or administrative
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Certiorari to the TS against TA rulings on guilty-plea certiorari, jurisdicción voluntaria, or administrative revisión: 30 days from Archivo en autos of the copy of the notice (or of the ruling on reconsideration) (Regla 20(a)(2), (3), (5) Reglamento TS). Jurisdictional.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Certiorari to the TS against other TA rulings in discretionary recursos, or TA interlocutory resolutions
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Certiorari to the TS against other TA rulings in discretionary recursos, or TA interlocutory resolutions: 30 days from Archivo en autos of the copy of the notice (Civ. Rule 52.2(b) says “fecha de notificación”) (Regla 20(b)(1) Reglamento TS; Regla 52.2(b) R. Proc. Civ.). Strict compliance. In criminal cases, Rule 217 R. Proc. Crim. calls the 30-day term for certiorari against a TA judgment or final resolution denying certiorari jurisdictional; treat it as jurisdictional.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Direct appeal to the TS (unconstitutionality or conflicting TA decisions)
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Direct appeal to the TS (unconstitutionality or conflicting TA decisions): 30 days from Archivo en autos of the copy of the notice of the TA judgment (or of the ruling on reconsideration) (Regla 17(a) Reglamento TS). Jurisdictional. 60 days in civil cases where the government is a party.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Notify the TA of a recurso filed in the TS
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Notify the TA of a recurso filed in the TS: 72 hours days from Filing in the TS (Reglas 17(b) y 20(d) Reglamento TS). Strict compliance. Stamped copy without the appendix.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Opposition to certiorari (TS)
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Opposition to certiorari (TS): 10 days from Notification of the petition (Regla 20(l) Reglamento TS). 25 pages.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Briefs in the TS after the writ issues or the appeal is accepted
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Briefs in the TS after the writ issues or the appeal is accepted: 30, then 30 days from Receipt of the Secretaría’s notice that the record was received (Regla 35(c)); then receipt of the petitioner’s or appellant’s brief (Reglas 19, 21 y 33(i) Reglamento TS). Regla 33(i) counts the second 30 days from filing of the other side’s brief; Reglas 19 and 21 from receipt. Use the earlier date.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Reconsideration in the TS
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Reconsideration in the TS: 10 business days days from Date the decision was sent to the parties (Regla 45(a)–(b) Reglamento TS). Jurisdictional; 10 pages; no extensions. A second motion only within 3 business days after notice of the denial.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — Electoral certiorari to the TS
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. Electoral certiorari to the TS: 10 days from Archivo en autos of the copy of the notice of the TA judgment (or of the ruling on reconsideration) (Regla 22(a) Reglamento TS). Jurisdictional. Reconsideration within 3 days. The TS rule still cites the 2011 Electoral Code; the Reglamento TA (Regla 41) refers to it as “Regla 21” of the Reglamento TS.

docs.t: Puerto Rico appeal deadline — TA mandate to the TPI or agency
docs.x: Puerto Rico appellate deadline. TA mandate to the TPI or agency: 10 business days days from The TA decision becoming final and firm (Regla 84(E) Reglamento TA). Since 2025 the TA may send it earlier for cause.

docs.t: Rhode Island — 20 days to appeal, and the Supreme Court cannot extend it
docs.x: Rhode Island land mine. 20 days to appeal, and the Supreme Court cannot extend it: A civil notice of appeal, with the $150 filing fee, must be filed in the trial court within 20 days of entry of the judgment, order, or decree (not 30). Only the trial court may extend, for excusable neglect, by no more than 30 days past the original deadline; the Supreme Court has no power to extend the time to appeal. (Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 4(a), 20(b))

docs.t: Rhode Island — Post-trial motions are due in 10 days, and only some stop the appeal clock
docs.x: Rhode Island land mine. Post-trial motions are due in 10 days, and only some stop the appeal clock: Renewed motions for judgment as a matter of law, motions to amend findings, new-trial motions, and motions to alter or amend must be served within 10 days after entry of judgment, and the time cannot be extended. Only those four motions restart the 20-day appeal period. A Rule 60(b) motion does not. (Super.R.Civ.P. 6(b), 50(b), 52(b), 59(b), (e); Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 4(a))

docs.t: Rhode Island — District Court civil appeals: 2 business days
docs.x: Rhode Island land mine. District Court civil appeals: 2 business days: To get a de novo trial in Superior Court after a District Court civil judgment, a party must file a written claim of appeal with the District Court clerk within 2 days after entry of judgment, excluding weekends and legal holidays, and pay the costs, including a $50 attorney’s fee for the other side, at that time. (R.I. Gen. Laws § 9-12-10)

docs.t: Rhode Island — 12% interest from accrual changes settlement math
docs.x: Rhode Island land mine. 12% interest from accrual changes settlement math: Prejudgment interest at 12% a year runs from the date the cause of action accrued and is added by the clerk; post-judgment interest is also 12%, accruing on the prejudgment interest as well. Each year between accrual and judgment adds about 12% of the damages award. (R.I. Gen. Laws § 9-21-10(a))

docs.t: Rhode Island — Arbitration certificate within 3 days and a 30-day rejection window
docs.x: Rhode Island land mine. Arbitration certificate within 3 days and a 30-day rejection window: Money cases of $100,000 or less are diverted to court-annexed arbitration. Counsel must file the arbitration certificate within 3 days after the last responsive pleading. Missing the 30-day deadline to file a written rejection (with $300) after the award is filed means judgment enters on the award. (Super. Ct. R. Governing Arbitration of Civil Actions 1(a), (e), 5)

docs.t: Rhode Island — Pro hac vice: 3 cases per 5 years, and local counsel in the room
docs.x: Rhode Island land mine. Pro hac vice: 3 cases per 5 years, and local counsel in the room: Nonresident lawyers are limited to 3 Rhode Island pro hac vice cases in 5 years unless the Supreme Court waives it, and admission is for ‘special and infrequent’ occasions based on client need. Rhode Island counsel must sign every paper and attend every hearing and trial day, ready to proceed alone, unless excused. (Sup. Ct. Art. II, R. 9(a); Super.R.Civ.P. 85)

docs.t: Rhode Island — Slander has a 1-year statute of limitations
docs.x: Rhode Island land mine. Slander has a 1-year statute of limitations: Claims for words spoken must be filed within 1 year after the words were spoken. Personal-injury claims get 3 years. (R.I. Gen. Laws § 9-1-14(a)-(b))

docs.t: Rhode Island — Uncontested-motion trap: object 3 days before the hearing
docs.x: Rhode Island land mine. Uncontested-motion trap: object 3 days before the hearing: Motions to amend, compel, for protective orders, to consolidate, to add third parties, for Rule 35 exams, to enlarge time after a deadline, and to assign are granted as a matter of course and never reach the calendar unless a written objection stating particular grounds is served and filed at least 3 days before the hearing. The extra day for electronic service does not apply. (Super.R.Civ.P. 7(b)(3))

docs.t: Rhode Island — Discovery runs on Rhode Island numbers, not federal ones
docs.x: Rhode Island land mine. Discovery runs on Rhode Island numbers, not federal ones: No initial disclosures. Interrogatory answers and document responses are due in 40 days (a defendant gets 60 days after service of process for document requests), with a 30-interrogatory cap. A plaintiff needs leave to serve interrogatories within 60 days after service of process. Untimely interrogatory objections are waived. Supplemental interrogatory answers are due no later than 30 days before trial. An order compelling discovery can provide for automatic dismissal or default if not obeyed within 30 days. (Super.R.Civ.P. 26, 33(a)-(c), 34(b)(2), 37(a)(4)(A))

docs.t: Rhode Island — Do not plead a dollar amount in injury cases
docs.x: Rhode Island land mine. Do not plead a dollar amount in injury cases: In actions for personal injury, property damage, or wrongful death, the complaint must not state the amount claimed, only that it is enough for the court’s jurisdiction. (Super.R.Civ.P. 8(a))

docs.t: Rhode Island — Miss the Rule 12A statement and the appeal is conditionally dismissed
docs.x: Rhode Island land mine. Miss the Rule 12A statement and the appeal is conditionally dismissed: The Rule 12A statement is due 20 days after the appeal is docketed. If it is late, the Clerk enters a conditional dismissal that becomes final unless the statement or an extension motion is filed within 10 days. A late appellee counter-statement or brief leads to a conditional default barring further filings and argument. (Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 12A(1)-(2), 18A)

docs.t: Rhode Island — Supreme Court briefs need 9 paper copies within 5 days
docs.x: Rhode Island land mine. Supreme Court briefs need 9 paper copies within 5 days: Even with mandatory e-filing, parties must deliver 9 paper copies of Rule 12A statements and briefs (6 of appendices, writ petitions, reargument petitions, and supporting memoranda) within 5 days after the Clerk accepts the electronic filing. Briefs must be in 14-point Times New Roman, double-spaced, with a signed word-count certification and the Clerk’s ‘Checklist for Filing Briefs’; a brief without the checklist is rejected. (Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 16(f), 18(b), (h))

docs.t: Rhode Island anti-SLAPP — Statute: R.I. Gen. Laws ch. 9-33 (conditional immunity, not a dismissal framework)
docs.x: Rhode Island anti-SLAPP. Statute: R.I. Gen. Laws ch. 9-33 (conditional immunity, not a dismissal framework): Rhode Island’s 1993 anti-SLAPP law makes a party’s exercise of the right of petition or free speech, under the U.S. or Rhode Island constitutions, in connection with a matter of public concern, conditionally immune from civil claims, counterclaims, and cross-claims directed at that activity. Covered activity is defined as any written or oral statement (1) made before or submitted to a legislative, executive, or judicial body or other governmental proceeding, (2) made in connection with an issue under consideration by such a body, or (3) made in connection with an issue of public concern. The legislative findings say such suits should be resolved quickly and at minimum cost to the citizen. (R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 9-33-1, 9-33-2(a), (e))

docs.t: Rhode Island anti-SLAPP — The only exception: ‘sham’ petitioning or speech, tested two ways
docs.x: Rhode Island anti-SLAPP. The only exception: ‘sham’ petitioning or speech, tested two ways: Immunity is lost only if the speech or petition is a sham, meaning it is not genuinely aimed at procuring a favorable government action, result, or outcome. It is a sham only if it is BOTH objectively baseless (no reasonable person could realistically expect success in procuring the government action) AND subjectively baseless (an attempt to use the governmental process itself, rather than its outcome, for its own direct effects). The statute’s sham test is framed around petitioning government. How it applies to speech on a public issue that is not aimed at any government body is not answered by the statutory text; check Rhode Island case law. (R.I. Gen. Laws § 9-33-2(a)(1)-(2))

docs.t: Rhode Island anti-SLAPP — Procedure: no special motion form, no deadline, automatic discovery stay
docs.x: Rhode Island anti-SLAPP. Procedure: no special motion form, no deadline, automatic discovery stay: Immunity may be raised by an appropriate motion or by other appropriate means under the civil rules. The statute sets no filing deadline and no hearing deadline. Filing a motion asserting the immunity automatically stays all discovery until notice of entry of the order ruling on it. The court may allow specified discovery only on motion, after a hearing, for good cause. (R.I. Gen. Laws § 9-33-2(b)-(c))

docs.t: Rhode Island anti-SLAPP — Fees are mandatory for the winner; damages if the suit was frivolous or meant to harass
docs.x: Rhode Island anti-SLAPP. Fees are mandatory for the winner; damages if the suit was frivolous or meant to harass: If the court grants the immunity motion, or the speaker or petitioner ultimately prevails at trial, the court must award costs and reasonable attorney’s fees, including those for the motion and related discovery. The court must also award compensatory damages, and may award punitive damages, if the prevailing party shows the claims were frivolous or brought to harass or otherwise inhibit petitioning or speech. Other remedies remain available. (R.I. Gen. Laws § 9-33-2(d))

docs.t: Rhode Island anti-SLAPP — Intervention by government and the Attorney General; other protections preserved
docs.x: Rhode Island anti-SLAPP. Intervention by government and the Attorney General; other protections preserved: The government agency or subdivision to which the petition or speech was directed, or the Attorney General, may intervene to defend or support the speaker. The chapter does not limit other constitutional, statutory, or common-law protections. (R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 9-33-3, 9-33-4)

docs.t: Rhode Island anti-SLAPP — Appeal of a denial: the statute is silent
docs.x: Rhode Island anti-SLAPP. Appeal of a denial: the statute is silent: Chapter 9-33 has no appeal provision, and a denial of an immunity motion is not among the interlocutory orders made appealable by R.I. Gen. Laws § 9-24-7 (injunctions, receivers, ordered sales, and new-trial orders after a jury trial). Review before final judgment would have to come by petition for certiorari to the Supreme Court under Article I, Rule 13. Whether the Supreme Court routinely grants such review is a case-law question not answered by the collected texts. (R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 9-33-2, 9-24-7; Sup. Ct. Art. I, R. 13)

docs.x: South Carolina land mine. docs.x: South Carolina land mine. docs.t: South Carolina anti-SLAPP — What a speech defendant can use instead
docs.x: South Carolina anti-SLAPP. What a speech defendant can use instead: Without an anti-SLAPP statute, the tools are an ordinary Rule 12(b)(6) motion (the SC wording is failure ’to state facts sufficient to constitute a cause of action’), summary judgment under Rule 56, Rule 11 sanctions, and the Frivolous Civil Proceedings Sanctions Act. Under the Act, after a verdict or a dismissal by directed verdict, summary judgment, or JNOV, the prevailing party may move for sanctions against a frivolous claim. The test is what a reasonable attorney would believe, proof is by a preponderance, and the person accused gets notice and 30 days to respond. Unlike anti-SLAPP fee shifting, this does not end the case early and does not shift fees automatically. (Rules 11, 12(b)(6), 56, SCRCP; S.C. Code § 15-36-10(A)(4), (C), (D))

docs.x: South Carolina appellate deadline. Order transcript (civil): 10 days from Service of notice of appeal (Rule 207(a)(1), SCACR). 30 days in General Sessions and juvenile appeals.

docs.x: South Carolina appellate deadline. Return to certiorari petition: 30 days from Service of the petition (Rule 242(f), SCACR). Reply due 10 days after service of return.

docs.x: South Dakota land mine. Interlocutory review: 10 days from notice of entry: Most pretrial orders are reviewable only by a petition for permission to appeal. docs.x: South Dakota land mine. Short-time periods skip weekends; e-service after midnight slips a day: For periods under 11 days, intermediate Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays are excluded. docs.x: South Dakota land mine. docs.x: South Dakota land mine. docs.x: South Dakota anti-SLAPP. Procedure: 60-day motion, automatic stay, 60-day hearing and ruling: File a special motion for expedited relief within 60 days after service of the pleading asserting the claim, or later for good cause. Filing stays all other proceedings between the movant and the respondent, including discovery, until the motion is decided and the time to appeal expires. The court may allow limited discovery if specific information is needed and not otherwise available. The court must hear the motion within 60 days after filing (later only for limited discovery or good cause) and rule within 60 days after the hearing. Unrelated motions, public-safety injunctions, fee motions, voluntary dismissals and severance are not stayed. (SDCL 15-40-3, 15-40-4, 15-40-5, 15-40-6, 15-40-7, 15-40-10)

docs.t: South Dakota anti-SLAPP — Standard: dismissal with prejudice
docs.x: South Dakota anti-SLAPP. Standard: dismissal with prejudice: The court considers the pleadings, motion papers and any evidence admissible on summary judgment. It must dismiss with prejudice if: the movant shows the chapter applies; the respondent fails to show an exclusion; and either the respondent fails to establish a prima facie case on each essential element, or the movant shows failure to state a claim or no genuine issue of material fact. A voluntary dismissal without prejudice does not defeat the motion or the fee claim, and a voluntary dismissal with prejudice means the movant prevailed. (SDCL 15-40-8, 15-40-9)

docs.t: South Dakota anti-SLAPP — Mandatory fees and immediate appeal
docs.x: South Dakota anti-SLAPP. Mandatory fees and immediate appeal: A prevailing movant must be awarded court costs, reasonable attorney fees and reasonable litigation expenses related to the motion. A prevailing respondent gets them only if the court finds the motion frivolous or filed solely to delay. A movant may appeal an order denying the motion in whole or in part as of right, within 30 days after entry of the order, and an appeal stays all proceedings between all parties until it ends. (SDCL 15-40-11, 15-40-12, 15-40-4)

docs.x: Virginia land mine. Post-trial motions do not extend the 21-day finality window or the 30-day appeal clock: A final judgment leaves the trial court’s control 21 days after the judge signs it. Filing a motion for a new trial or reconsideration does not extend that time or the time to note an appeal. Only an order that actually modifies, vacates or suspends the judgment within the 21 days does, and appeal time then runs from the new final judgment. Get a suspending order entered, not just a motion filed. (Rule 1:1(a); Rule 5A:3(a))

docs.x: Virginia land mine. Notice of appeal goes to the trial court clerk within 30 days, with the $50 fee and an appeal bond: The notice of appeal to the Court of Appeals must be filed with the clerk of the circuit court within 30 days after entry of the final judgment. A copy goes to the Court of Appeals clerk with the $50 fee (the appeal is dismissed if the fee does not arrive within 10 days). In an appeal of right in a civil case, a $500 appeal bond (or the amount the trial court sets) must be filed simultaneously. The bond is not jurisdictional, but missing it invites a motion. docs.x: Virginia land mine. The Court of Appeals can extend that only on a written motion filed within 90 days after entry. Notice of filing the transcript is due to all counsel within 10 days. docs.t: Virginia — Preliminary assignments of error are due 15 days after the record is filed
docs.x: Virginia land mine. docs.t: Vermont anti-SLAPP — 12 V.S.A. § 1041: special motion to strike
docs.x: Vermont anti-SLAPP. 12 V.S.A. § 1041: special motion to strike: Vermont’s anti-SLAPP statute lets a defendant file a special motion to strike a claim arising from the defendant’s exercise, in connection with a public issue, of the right of free speech or the right to petition the government under the U.S. or Vermont Constitution. Protected activity includes: statements made before a legislative, executive, or judicial proceeding or other official proceeding; statements made in connection with an issue under review by such a body; statements on an issue of public interest made in a public forum or a place open to the public; and any other statement or conduct on a public issue or issue of public interest that furthers free speech or petition rights. docs.t: Vermont anti-SLAPP — Deadline: 60 days from filing of the complaint; hearing within 30 days
docs.x: Vermont anti-SLAPP. Deadline: 60 days from filing of the complaint; hearing within 30 days: File and serve the motion within 60 days after the complaint is filed. The clock runs from filing, not from service. The plaintiff may respond within 15 days after service of the motion. The court may extend these times for good cause. The court must hold a hearing within 30 days after the motion is served, unless good cause supports an extension. (12 V.S.A. § 1041(b), (d))

docs.t: Vermont anti-SLAPP — Discovery stay
docs.x: Vermont anti-SLAPP. Discovery stay: Filing the motion stays all discovery in the action until the court rules. On motion and for good cause, the court may allow limited discovery to help it decide the motion. (12 V.S.A. § 1041(c))

docs.t: Vermont anti-SLAPP — Standard: plaintiff must show no reasonable basis AND actual injury
docs.x: Vermont anti-SLAPP. Standard: plaintiff must show no reasonable basis AND actual injury: The court must grant the motion unless the plaintiff shows both that (A) the defendant’s exercise of speech or petition rights was devoid of any reasonable factual support and any arguable basis in law, and (B) the defendant’s acts caused actual injury to the plaintiff. The court decides on the pleadings and on supporting and opposing affidavits. The ruling, and the fact that the court made it, are not admissible later in the case and do not change any burden or degree of proof. (12 V.S.A. § 1041(e), (f)(2))

docs.t: Vermont anti-SLAPP — Fees: mandatory for a winning defendant; two-way for frivolous motions
docs.x: Vermont anti-SLAPP. Fees: mandatory for a winning defendant; two-way for frivolous motions: If the motion is granted, the court must award costs and reasonable attorney’s fees to the defendant. If the motion is denied and the court finds it frivolous or meant only to cause delay, the court must award costs and fees to the plaintiff. Separately, 12 V.S.A. § 5771 lets the court award costs and fees to a defendant who wins a defamation action that it finds frivolous and without merit. (12 V.S.A. § 1041(f)(1); 12 V.S.A. § 5771)

docs.t: Vermont anti-SLAPP — Appeal; exclusions
docs.x: Vermont anti-SLAPP. Appeal; exclusions: An order granting or denying the motion is appealable in the same manner as an interlocutory order under V.R.A.P. 5. The statute does not say more. Check whether the appellate courts treat this as an appeal as of right or one that still requires the V.R.A.P. 5 permission procedure; case law was not collected. The statute does not apply to (1) enforcement actions or criminal proceedings brought by the State or a political subdivision, or (2) cases of tortious interference with legally protected health care under 12 V.S.A. § 7302. (12 V.S.A. § 1041(g), (h))

docs.x: Vermont appellate deadline. Notice of appeal (civil, and most agency appeals): 30 days from entry of the judgment or order (V.R.A.P. 4(a)(1); 12 V.S.A. § 2383). File with the superior court clerk or agency. Jurisdictional (2026 VT 13, ¶ 4).

docs.t: Wisconsin — Filing commences the case, but you have 90 days to serve, and that cannot be extended
docs.x: Wisconsin land mine. Filing commences the case, but you have 90 days to serve, and that cannot be extended: An action is commenced when the summons and complaint are filed, but only if an authenticated copy is served within 90 days after filing. The court cannot enlarge the 90 days. Service must be made with reasonable diligence; substitute service at the home and publication are allowed only after reasonable diligence fails at personal service. (Wis. Stat. §§ 801.02(1), 801.15(2)(a), 801.11(1))

docs.t: Wisconsin — Answer deadline is 20 days, or 45 days in tort, insurer, and state cases
docs.x: Wisconsin land mine. Answer deadline is 20 days, or 45 days in tort, insurer, and state cases: An answer is due 20 days after service of the complaint, but 45 days if any claim sounds in tort, if an insurance company is a defendant, or if the defendant is the state. The summons must state the correct period (20 or 45 days; 40 days after first publication if served by publication). The same 45-day rule applies to replies, motions to strike, and responses to amended pleadings. (Wis. Stat. §§ 801.09(2), 802.06(1), (6), 802.09(1))

docs.t: Wisconsin — Do not plead a dollar amount in a tort complaint
docs.x: Wisconsin land mine. Do not plead a dollar amount in a tort complaint: In a tort claim for money, the demand for judgment may not state the amount sought. You must disclose the amount to the court and other parties before a hearing on summary judgment or judgment on the pleadings, and before default or final judgment. (Wis. Stat. §§ 802.02(1m), 802.06(3), 802.08(2), 806.01(1)(c), 806.02(2))

docs.t: Wisconsin — Time computation: periods under 11 days skip weekends and holidays
docs.x: Wisconsin land mine. Time computation: periods under 11 days skip weekends and holidays: Exclude Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays (including a full day on Good Friday) when a period is less than 11 days. Add 3 days for mail service. Add 1 day for fax, email, or e-filing service only if completed between 5 p.m. and midnight. Late motions to enlarge need excusable neglect, and the court cannot extend the time to appeal, to decide post-verdict motions, or to move under s. 805.17(3) or s. 806.07. (Wis. Stat. § 801.15(1)-(2), (5))

docs.t: Wisconsin — 60-day window to substitute the judge
docs.x: Wisconsin land mine. 60-day window to substitute the judge: The peremptory substitution request must be filed within 60 days (plaintiff: from filing; others: from service) and before any preliminary contested matter is heard. Arguing a contested motion first forfeits it. (Wis. Stat. § 801.58(1))

docs.t: Wisconsin — Summary judgment within 8 months, and amend once within 6 months
docs.x: Wisconsin land mine. Summary judgment within 8 months, and amend once within 6 months: Absent a scheduling order, a summary judgment motion must be made within 8 months after the summons and complaint are filed, served at least 20 days before the hearing, with opposing affidavits at least 5 days before. A pleading may be amended once as of course only within 6 months after filing, and a third-party complaint may be served without leave only within 6 months. (Wis. Stat. §§ 802.08(1)-(2), 802.09(1), 803.05(1))

docs.t: Wisconsin — Discovery has hard caps and no initial disclosures
docs.x: Wisconsin land mine. Discovery has hard caps and no initial disclosures: Limits absent stipulation or order: 25 interrogatories including subparts; 10 depositions of no more than 7 hours each; document requests reaching back no more than 5 years before the claim accrued. There is no general initial-disclosure rule, but litigation-funding agreements must be produced unprompted. A motion to dismiss for failure to state a claim, for judgment on the pleadings, or for a more definite statement automatically stays discovery for up to 180 days. (Wis. Stat. §§ 804.08(1)(am), 804.045, 804.09(1), 804.01(2)(bg), 802.06(1)(b))

docs.t: Wisconsin — Jury: demand early, 5/6 verdict, special verdicts
docs.x: Wisconsin land mine. Jury: demand early, 5/6 verdict, special verdicts: Demand a jury at or before the scheduling or pretrial conference, whichever is first, and pay the fee on the scheduling order’s timetable, or the jury is waived. Five-sixths of the jurors decide, and the same five-sixths must agree on every question needed for a verdict on a claim. Special verdicts are the default. Failing to object at the instruction and verdict conference waives instruction and verdict errors. (Wis. Stat. §§ 805.01(2)-(3), 802.10(3)(e), 805.09(2), 805.12(1), 805.13(3))

docs.t: Wisconsin — Post-verdict motions: 20 days, then deemed denied at 90
docs.x: Wisconsin land mine. Post-verdict motions: 20 days, then deemed denied at 90: Motions after verdict must be filed and served within 20 days after the verdict unless the court sets a longer time within those 20 days. If not decided within 90 days after the verdict, they are deemed denied and judgment is entered. In bench trials, a motion to amend findings or the judgment is due 20 days after entry of judgment; undecided at 90 days, it is deemed denied and the appeal clock starts 90 days after entry. (Wis. Stat. §§ 805.16(1)-(3), 805.17(3))

docs.t: Wisconsin — Appeal deadline depends on notice of entry: 45 or 90 days, unextendable
docs.x: Wisconsin land mine. Appeal deadline depends on notice of entry: 45 or 90 days, unextendable: Appeal within 45 days of entry of the final judgment or order if written notice of entry is given within 21 days of entry; otherwise within 90 days. No court can enlarge it. Serving notice of entry within 21 days is how the winner shortens the loser’s time. Nonfinal orders require a petition for leave within 14 days. (Wis. Stat. §§ 808.04(1), 806.06(5), 809.82(2)(b), 809.50(1))

docs.t: Wisconsin — Email service needs written consent unless both sides e-file
docs.x: Wisconsin land mine. Email service needs written consent unless both sides e-file: Service of papers by email is allowed only if the recipient consented in writing; between registered e-filing users, the system’s notice of activity is service. Self-represented ‘paper parties’ must be served by traditional methods. Documents needing personal service still need it. (Wis. Stat. §§ 801.14(2), 801.18(6)(a)-(c))

docs.t: Wisconsin — Rule 11 safe harbor and a separate frivolous-claims statute
docs.x: Wisconsin land mine. Rule 11 safe harbor and a separate frivolous-claims statute: Sanctions under s. 802.05 have a 21-day safe harbor before filing the motion. Separately, s. 895.044 allows actual fees, on clear and convincing proof, for claims or defenses brought in bad faith or without reasonable basis, also with a 21-day withdrawal window. (Wis. Stat. §§ 802.05(3)(a)1., 895.044(2))

docs.t: Wisconsin anti-SLAPP — No anti-SLAPP statute in force
docs.x: Wisconsin anti-SLAPP. No anti-SLAPP statute in force: Wisconsin has no anti-SLAPP law. The statutes certified November 4, 2026 contain no special motion to dismiss for speech or petitioning (ch. 802 has no s. 802.065, and s. 895.69 is the structured-settlement transfer procedure, not an anti-SLAPP provision). The 2025–26 Legislature considered the Uniform Public Expression Protection Act (2025 A.B. 701 / S.B. 666), which would have created s. 802.065 and added it to the motion defenses in s. 802.06(2). A.B. 701 passed the Assembly on February 17, 2026, but both bills died in the Senate on March 23, 2026 under Senate Joint Resolution 1. Earlier 2023 bills also were not enacted. What a speech defendant can use instead: a motion to dismiss for failure to state a claim, which automatically stays discovery for up to 180 days (s. 802.06(1)(b)); the libel retraction-notice rule (s. 895.05(2));

docs.t: Wisconsin anti-SLAPP — Frivolous-claim fees (s. 895.044) are the closest fee tool
docs.x: Wisconsin anti-SLAPP. Frivolous-claim fees (s. 895.044) are the closest fee tool: A party or the party’s lawyer can be liable for actual costs and reasonable attorney fees for commencing, using, or continuing a claim, defense, or appeal that was brought in bad faith solely to harass or maliciously injure, or that the party or lawyer knew or should have known had no reasonable basis in law or equity. The court must find this by clear and convincing evidence. There is a 21-day safe harbor: if the challenged claim is withdrawn or corrected within 21 days after service of the motion, an award is discretionary; if not, the award is mandatory. (Wis. Stat. § 895.044(1)-(2))

docs.x: Wisconsin appellate deadline. Notice of appeal (final judgment or order), no notice of entry: 90 days from Entry of the final judgment or order (Wis. Stat. § 808.04(1)). Jurisdictional; cannot be enlarged.

docs.x: Wisconsin appellate deadline. Decision on motions after verdict (else deemed denied): 90 days from Verdict (Wis. Stat. § 805.16(3)). Cannot be enlarged (s. 801.15(2)(c)); judgment then entered on the verdict.

docs.x: Wisconsin appellate deadline. Motion to amend findings or judgment (bench trial): 20 days from Entry of judgment (Wis. Stat. § 805.17(3)). Deemed denied if undecided 90 days after entry; appeal time then runs from day 90.

docs.x: Wisconsin appellate deadline. Motion for 3-judge panel by a party other than appellant: 14 days from Service of the notice of appeal (Wis. Stat. § 809.41(1)(d)). Appellant must file with the notice of appeal; failure waives.

docs.x: Wisconsin appellate deadline. Reply brief or statement that none will be filed: 15 days from Later of service (+3 days if mailed) or filing of respondent’s brief (Wis. Stat. § 809.19(4)(a)). 3,000 words.

docs.t: West Virginia — The notice of appeal is filed with the appellate Clerk, not the circuit clerk, within 30 days
docs.x: West Virginia land mine. The notice of appeal is filed with the appellate Clerk, not the circuit clerk, within 30 days: Appeals from final civil judgments entered after June 30, 2022 go to the Intermediate Court of Appeals. File the Appendix A notice of appeal, with all required attachments including the order appealed, in the Office of the Clerk of the Supreme Court/Intermediate Court within 30 days of entry. Serve it on all parties, on the circuit clerk, and on each court reporter from whom a transcript is ordered. The appellate court may extend the notice deadline for good cause, but the 3-day mail rule never extends it. (RAP 5(b), 5(i)(1), 39(c); W. Va. Code § 51-11-4(b)(1))

docs.t: West Virginia — The appeal is “perfected” by the opening brief and appendix within four months, with at most two months’ extension
docs.x: West Virginia land mine. The appeal is “perfected” by the opening brief and appendix within four months, with at most two months’ extension: Unless law provides otherwise, the petitioner must file the brief and the appendix record within four months of entry of the judgment. Total extensions may not exceed two months, and failure to perfect results in dismissal. There is no automatic transmission of the record; the petitioner builds and files the appendix. (RAP 5(f)–(g), 5(i)(2), 6(c), 7, 10(b))

docs.t: West Virginia — No interlocutory appeals to the Intermediate Court
docs.x: West Virginia land mine. No interlocutory appeals to the Intermediate Court: The Intermediate Court has no jurisdiction over interlocutory appeals, certified questions or extraordinary writs. A non-final order is reviewed by petition for a writ of prohibition in the Supreme Court, which is discretionary and “sparingly exercised”, or by a certified question under § 58-5-2. A partial judgment is appealable only with an express Rule 54(b) no-just-reason-for-delay determination. The notice of appeal form makes you explain finality. (W. Va. Code §§ 51-11-4(d)(8)–(10), 58-5-1(a), 58-5-2; RAP 1(b), 16(a); W. Va. R. Civ. P. 54(b))

docs.t: West Virginia — After a jury trial, skipping a new-trial motion waives trial errors
docs.x: West Virginia land mine. After a jury trial, skipping a new-trial motion waives trial errors: A party that does not file a timely Rule 59 new-trial motion after a jury verdict is deemed to have waived all trial errors it could have raised in that motion. A denied Rule 50(b) motion is the only exception. The motion is due 28 days after entry of judgment and cannot be extended. (W. Va. R. Civ. P. 59(b), 59(f), 6(b)(2))

docs.t: West Virginia — Local counsel must have a West Virginia office and must show up, including at depositions
docs.x: West Virginia land mine. Local counsel must have a West Virginia office and must show up, including at depositions: Pro hac vice requires association with a West Virginia lawyer whose primary daily office is physically in West Virginia. That lawyer must sign every served paper (unsigned papers are invalid) and attend every hearing, trial and deposition unless the judge permits remote attendance. Budget $350 per lawyer per case plus a $350 annual fee, and a fresh application for any appeal. (W. Va. R. Admission 8.0(b), (c), (e), (f); RAP 3(c))

docs.t: West Virginia — Judge-disqualification motions have short windows and a verified certificate
docs.x: West Virginia land mine. Judge-disqualification motions have short windows and a verified certificate: There is no peremptory strike of a judge. A disqualification motion must be filed within 30 days of learning the ground, at least 7 days before a hearing or 21 days before trial, cite the specific Rule 2.11 ground, and carry a verified certificate of counsel. A late motion can be decided by the challenged judge, and rulings are not immediately appealable. (TCR 17.01, 17.05, 17.07)

docs.t: West Virginia — Answers are due in 30 days, but motion responses in 21 days and hearing notices 14 days ahead
docs.x: West Virginia land mine. Answers are due in 30 days, but motion responses in 21 days and hearing notices 14 days ahead: Defendants answer in 30 days after service (and must attach a civil case information statement). By contrast: - motion response memoranda are due 21 days after service of the motion; - replies are due 7 days after the response; - a motion and notice of hearing must be served at least 14 days before the hearing; - supporting memoranda are capped at 20 pages without leave; - no pleading may be filed less than 48 hours before oral presentation or argument without permission. (W. Va. R. Civ. P. 6(d), 12(a)(1); TCR 6.01(c), 22.01)

docs.t: West Virginia — Do not count on three extra days after e-service
docs.x: West Virginia land mine. Do not count on three extra days after e-service: RCP 6(e) adds three days only after service by mail, by leaving the paper with the clerk, or by other consented means; e-service under the Trial Court Rules (RCP 5(b)(2)(E)) is not listed. TCR 15A.18 says e-service is “treated the same as service by mail” for Rules of Civil Procedure purposes. Until that conflict is resolved, calendar from the e-service date. On appeal, the 3-day mail addition never applies to docketing or perfecting deadlines or to court-ordered dates. (W. Va. R. Civ. P. 5(b)(2)(E), 6(e); TCR 15A.18; RAP 39(c))

docs.t: West Virginia — Six-person civil juries, two peremptories per side, and a 14-day jury demand
docs.x: West Virginia land mine. Six-person civil juries, two peremptories per side, and a 14-day jury demand: A civil jury has six members unless the court orders more. Each side gets two peremptory challenges, exercised alternately starting with the plaintiff, and multiple parties on a side may be treated as one. A jury demand must be served within 14 days after the last pleading on the issue and filed, or the jury is waived. (W. Va. R. Civ. P. 38(b), (d), 47(b), 48)

docs.t: West Virginia — Summary judgment motions are cut off 30 days after discovery closes
docs.x: West Virginia land mine. Summary judgment motions are cut off 30 days after discovery closes: Unless the court sets a different time, a summary-judgment motion may be filed only until 30 days after the close of all discovery. The court must state findings of fact and conclusions of law when it grants the motion, a common basis for reversal. (W. Va. R. Civ. P. 56(b), 52(a)(3))

docs.t: West Virginia — Election days are legal holidays, and the trial and appellate holiday lists differ
docs.x: West Virginia land mine. Election days are legal holidays, and the trial and appellate holiday lists differ: Under RCP 6, any day on which a general, special or primary election is held statewide or in the county is a legal holiday, as are Lincoln’s Birthday and West Virginia Day. The appellate holiday list in RAP 39 adds Juneteenth, which RCP 6 does not list unless declared by the Governor or President. RAP 39 also excludes weekends and holidays from periods under seven days, while RCP 6 counts every day. (W. Va. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(1), (a)(6); RAP 39(a))

docs.t: West Virginia — Cases idle for a year can be dismissed
docs.x: West Virginia land mine. Cases idle for a year can be dismissed: A circuit court may dismiss any action pending more than one year in which the plaintiff has taken no action, after notice and an opportunity to be heard. Reinstatement requires good cause on a motion filed within three terms of court after the dismissal order. Actions may also be dismissed for unpaid accrued court costs. (W. Va. R. Civ. P. 41(b)(2)–(4); TCR 2)

docs.t: West Virginia anti-SLAPP — No anti-SLAPP statute; the 2025 UPEPA bill died in committee
docs.x: West Virginia anti-SLAPP. No anti-SLAPP statute; the 2025 UPEPA bill died in committee: West Virginia has not enacted an anti-SLAPP law. House Bill 3205 of the 2025 Regular Session (“Uniform Public Expression Protection”) was introduced and referred to House Judiciary on March 6, 2025, and that is its last recorded action. The 2026 Regular Session bill list shows no public-expression or anti-SLAPP bill. The only related item found was SB 668 (“Providing compensation to victims of abusive lawsuits”), referred to Senate Judiciary on January 29, 2026 with no further action; its text was not reviewed. The Code’s Chapter 55 (civil remedies) has no such article; its articles end at Article 21 (commercial receiverships). How this was checked: the Legislature’s 2025 and 2026 all-bills lists (searched for “public expression”, “SLAPP” and “strategic lawsuit”), the HB 3205 and SB 668 history pages,

docs.t: West Virginia anti-SLAPP — What a defendant uses instead
docs.x: West Virginia anti-SLAPP. What a defendant uses instead: There is no special motion, discovery stay or fee-shifting for speech-based suits. Defenses come through ordinary procedure: a Rule 12(b)(6) motion (on which the court must state findings and conclusions when it grants the motion, RCP 52(a)(3)); summary judgment, which may be filed until 30 days after discovery closes (RCP 56(b)); Rule 11 sanctions after the 21-day safe harbor; and protective orders under RCP 26(c). Denial of a motion to dismiss cannot be appealed to the Intermediate Court because it has no interlocutory jurisdiction. The routes are a certified question under W. Va. Code § 58-5-2 (which covers denied summary-judgment motions and pleading-sufficiency questions) or a writ of prohibition in the Supreme Court (RAP 16). (W. Va. R. Civ. P. 11(c), 12(b), 26(c), 52(a)(3), 56(b); W. Va. Code §§ 51-11-4(d)(8), 58-5-2; RAP 16

docs.t: West Virginia appeal deadline — Notice of appeal (circuit court final order to Intermediate Court)
docs.x: West Virginia appellate deadline. Notice of appeal (circuit court final order to Intermediate Court): 30 days from entry of the final order (RAP 5(b)). Filed with the appellate Clerk; extendable for good cause (RAP 5(i)(1)); no 3-day mail extension (RAP 39(c)).

docs.t: West Virginia appeal deadline — Notice of appeal to the Supreme Court from the Intermediate Court
docs.x: West Virginia appellate deadline. Notice of appeal to the Supreme Court from the Intermediate Court: 30 days from entry of the Intermediate Court’s mandate (RAP 5(b); W. Va. Code § 51-11-10). Attach the mandate; review is discretionary.

docs.t: West Virginia appeal deadline — Motion for direct review in the Supreme Court
docs.x: West Virginia appellate deadline. Motion for direct review in the Supreme Court: 20 days from filing of the notice of appeal in the Intermediate Court (RAP 29(f); W. Va. Code § 51-11-5(a)). Response due 10 days after filing.

docs.t: West Virginia appeal deadline — Perfect the appeal (petitioner’s brief and appendix)
docs.x: West Virginia appellate deadline. Perfect the appeal (petitioner’s brief and appendix): 120 days from entry of the judgment appealed (RAP 5(f), 10(b)). Rule states four months, not 120 days; total extensions capped at two months (RAP 5(i)(2)).

docs.t: West Virginia appeal deadline — Respondent’s brief
docs.x: West Virginia appellate deadline. Respondent’s brief: 45 days from filing of the petitioner’s brief (RAP 10(b)). Typical schedule; the scheduling order controls.

docs.t: West Virginia appeal deadline — Reply brief
docs.x: West Virginia appellate deadline. Reply brief: 20 days from filing of the respondent’s brief (RAP 10(b), 10(g)). 30 days if the response contains cross-assignments of error.

docs.t: West Virginia appeal deadline — Respondent’s additional transcript request
docs.x: West Virginia appellate deadline. Respondent’s additional transcript request: 14 days from service of the notice of appeal (RAP 9(d)).

docs.t: West Virginia appeal deadline — Party designated as uninterested asks to remain a party
docs.x: West Virginia appellate deadline. Party designated as uninterested asks to remain a party: 20 days from filing of the notice of appeal (RAP 5(c)).

docs.t: West Virginia appeal deadline — Respondent’s additions to appendix list
docs.x: West Virginia appellate deadline. Respondent’s additions to appendix list: 10 days from receipt of the petitioner’s list (RAP 7(e)).

docs.t: West Virginia appeal deadline — Motion for disposition by memorandum decision
docs.x: West Virginia appellate deadline. Motion for disposition by memorandum decision: 20 days from perfection of the appeal (RAP 21(b)). Response due 10 days after filing.

docs.t: West Virginia appeal deadline — Response to a motion
docs.x: West Virginia appellate deadline. Response to a motion: 10 days from filing of the motion (RAP 29(a)). Replies need leave; expedited-relief responses are due in 2 days (RAP 29(c)).

docs.t: West Virginia appeal deadline — Continuance or waiver of oral argument
docs.x: West Virginia appellate deadline. Continuance or waiver of oral argument: 10 days from date of the notice of argument (RAP 19(c), (f); 20(c), (f)).

docs.t: West Virginia appeal deadline — Petition for rehearing
docs.x: West Virginia appellate deadline. Petition for rehearing: 30 days from release of the opinion or memorandum decision (RAP 25(a)). Response optional, due 14 days after the petition.

docs.t: West Virginia appeal deadline — Mandate issues
docs.x: West Virginia appellate deadline. Mandate issues: 30 days from release of the decision (if no rehearing petition) (RAP 26(b)). Within 7 days after denial of rehearing.

docs.t: West Virginia appeal deadline — Renewed JMOL / new trial / alter or amend / amend findings
docs.x: West Virginia appellate deadline. Renewed JMOL / new trial / alter or amend / amend findings: 28 days from entry of judgment (W. Va. R. Civ. P. 50(b), 52(b), 59(b), (e)). Not extendable (Rule 6(b)(2)); effect on appeal time not stated in the collected rules.

docs.t: West Virginia appeal deadline — Family court appeal to the Intermediate Court: notice / perfection
docs.x: West Virginia appellate deadline. Family court appeal to the Intermediate Court: notice / perfection: 30 days from entry of the family court order (RAP 13(c)(1), (3)). Perfect within 60 days; respondent 15 days and reply 10 days after; direct Supreme Court appeal requires both parties’ notice within 14 days (RAP 13(b)).

docs.t: West Virginia appeal deadline — Motion to disqualify a circuit judge
docs.x: West Virginia appellate deadline. Motion to disqualify a circuit judge: 30 days from discovery of the ground (TCR 17.01(a)). And at least 7 days before a hearing or 21 days before trial.

docs.t: Wyoming — Peremptory strike of the judge: plaintiff gets 14 days; defendant must use it by the first response
docs.x: Wyoming land mine. Peremptory strike of the judge: plaintiff gets 14 days; defendant must use it by the first response: Out-of-state lawyers often expect no peremptory challenge, or a longer window. In Wyoming a plaintiff must move within 14 days after the clerk’s notice of assignment (or of a reassignment). A defendant must move by its first responsive pleading or Rule 12 motion, or 14 days after a reassignment, whichever is later. A party gets one strike per case, and parties added later get none. (W.R.C.P. 40.1(b)(1))

docs.t: Wyoming — Post-judgment motions are deemed denied at 90 days, and the appeal clock starts then
docs.x: Wyoming land mine. Post-judgment motions are deemed denied at 90 days, and the appeal clock starts then: A Rule 50(b), 52(b), 59, or 60(b) motion not decided within 90 days after filing is deemed denied, unless the court enters an order continuing it, for no more than 60 days. The 30 days to appeal then run from the deemed denial, not from any later ruling. A judge who rules after the deemed-denial date has lost jurisdiction to decide the motion. (W.R.C.P. 6(c)(4); W.R.A.P. 2.01(a), 2.02(b))

docs.t: Wyoming — Notice of appeal: file in the trial court, serve the Supreme Court clerk, and attach the appendix list
docs.x: Wyoming land mine. Notice of appeal: file in the trial court, serve the Supreme Court clerk, and attach the appendix list: The notice of appeal is filed with the trial-court clerk within 30 days of entry of the appealable order, and that deadline is jurisdictional. A copy must also go to the appellate clerk at the same time. In civil cases the notice needs an appendix listing (not attaching) every pleading asserting a claim, every order disposing of claims or parties, and the judgment and any decision letter. The notice must also carry a certificate about ordering the transcript. Missing pieces bring monetary sanctions when the appeal is docketed. The docket fee is paid to the trial-court clerk when the notice is filed. (W.R.A.P. 1.03, 2.01(a), 2.05(a), 2.07, 2.09(a))

docs.t: Wyoming — Pro hac vice does not travel, and you cannot e-file
docs.x: Wyoming land mine. Pro hac vice does not travel, and you cannot e-file: Trial-court pro hac vice admission does not admit you in the Supreme Court; a new motion is required. Every admission requires a separate Wyoming State Bar application and Rule 8 certificate for each case. Pro hac vice counsel cannot e-file in the trial courts, so local counsel files everything. (W.R.A.P. 19.01(c); Rules Governing the Wyo. State Bar R. 8(c)-(d); Wyo. R. Elec. Filing & Serv. 4(b)(1))

docs.t: Wyoming — A Wyoming lawyer must attend every hearing
docs.x: Wyoming land mine. A Wyoming lawyer must attend every hearing: An active Wyoming Bar member must attend all hearings of any represented party unless the court excuses it after notice to other counsel. For pro hac vice matters, local counsel must be present at all proceedings, with full authority. Budget for local counsel at every setting, including pretrial conferences. (U.R.D.C. 101(c), 104(f)(3))

docs.t: Wyoming — Counsel cannot stipulate to extensions or continuances
docs.x: Wyoming land mine. Counsel cannot stipulate to extensions or continuances: Unlike common practice elsewhere, Wyoming counsel cannot extend rule- or order-based deadlines by agreement. Only a court order does it, except where the W.R.C.P. allow otherwise. One exception: a timely, one-time clerk’s extension of up to 15 days to answer, or to respond to interrogatories, document requests, or requests for admission. (U.R.D.C. 201, 202; W.R.C.P. 6(b)(3))

docs.t: Wyoming — No discovery until initial disclosures are done, and there is no automatic Rule 26(f) conference
docs.x: Wyoming land mine. No discovery until initial disclosures are done, and there is no automatic Rule 26(f) conference: Initial disclosures are due within 30 days after the answer is due. No party may seek discovery from any source until that period has run and the party has made its own disclosures. Wyoming has no mandatory early meet-and-confer; a discovery conference happens only if the court orders it or a party moves for one. (W.R.C.P. 26(a)(1.3), 26(d)(1), 26(f))

docs.t: Wyoming — Voluntary dismissal no longer gets the savings statute (since September 21, 2026)
docs.x: Wyoming land mine. Voluntary dismissal no longer gets the savings statute (since September 21, 2026): Under amended Rule 41, a voluntary dismissal is not a ‘failure otherwise than upon the merits’ under W.S. 1-3-118. Do not dismiss voluntarily and plan to refile under the savings statute after limitations has run. (W.R.C.P. 41(a)(3) (eff. Sept. 21, 2026))

docs.t: Wyoming — Contingent fee agreements must use Wyoming’s form
docs.x: Wyoming land mine. Contingent fee agreements must use Wyoming’s form: A standard engagement letter from another state will not comply. Wyoming requires an agreement in duplicate, signed by the lawyer and each client, substantially in the prescribed form, with a copy of the contingent fee rules given to and explained to the client. Changes that affect the client’s rights need district-court approval. Each fee-sharing lawyer is liable for the others’ malpractice as if partners. (Rules Governing Contingent Fees R. 4, 5(d)-(e), 6; Wyo. R. Prof. Conduct 1.5(b))

docs.t: Wyoming — Costs and fees: two short clocks after judgment
docs.x: Wyoming land mine. Costs and fees: two short clocks after judgment: Under W.R.C.P. 54(d), costs other than attorney’s fees and claims for attorney’s fees both require a motion within 21 days after entry of judgment. U.R.D.C. 501(a) also requires an itemized certificate of costs within 20 days after entry of a final judgment allowing costs, and objections are due within 10 days. File by the earlier date and satisfy both. U.R.D.C. 501(a)(3)(B) limits taxable witness fees to $30 a day, plus mileage at $.23 a mile. Expert fees are limited to $25 a day unless the court allows more. (W.R.C.P. 54(d)(1)-(2); U.R.D.C. 501(a))

docs.t: Wyoming — Answer in 20 days and serve within 90
docs.x: Wyoming land mine. Answer in 20 days and serve within 90: A defendant served in Wyoming answers within 20 days, or 30 days if served outside Wyoming or by publication. A plaintiff who has not served a defendant within 90 days after filing faces dismissal without prejudice under W.R.C.P. 4(w) and U.R.D.C. 203(b). (W.R.C.P. 4(w), 12(a)(1)(A); U.R.D.C. 203(b))

docs.t: Wyoming — Chancery court means no jury
docs.x: Wyoming land mine. Chancery court means no jury: Removing a business case to chancery court (or filing there) waives a jury, because the court uses only nonjury trials. Removal from district court requires every party’s written consent within 60 days after service on the last defendant. (W.S. 5-13-115(a); W.R.C.P. 3.2(a))

docs.t: Wyoming anti-SLAPP — No anti-SLAPP statute in force
docs.x: Wyoming anti-SLAPP. No anti-SLAPP statute in force: Wyoming has no anti-SLAPP law: no special motion to dismiss, no discovery stay, and no fee-shifting tied to speech or petitioning. Title 1 of the Wyoming Statutes (civil procedure), in the legislature’s compilation dated May 2026, ends at chapter 43 (Mediation). It has no chapter on lawsuits against public participation, and neither ‘SLAPP’ nor ‘public participation’ appears anywhere in it. The Legislative Service Office’s April 20, 2026 memo to the Joint Judiciary Committee says 39 states had anti-SLAPP laws as of April 2026. It names Idaho, Montana, South Dakota, and Utah among the states that adopted the Uniform Public Expression Protection Act, and it does not list Wyoming.
